newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Harvey Nichols sees strong H2.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Harvey Nichols sees strong H2.

text.p: High class fashion store Harvey Nichols Plc, which saw profits jump 35 pct in the first half, said on Thursday it was optimistic about prospects for trading for the rest of its financial year.
"We expect strong trading to continue," finance director Clive Morton said in a telephone interview.

He attributed the store's consistent growth over the past four years to management focus, buying the right stock and creating the right ambience for the store. He said the new Leeds store, which opened in October, was doing well, but had no news on plans to open stores in Manchester and Glasgow.

Morton said the group was looking for sites, but had nothing to announce at this stage. He said there were a couple of sites under consideration in London for expanding the company's restaurant business.

The store, which floated on the stockmarket earlier this year, already has a restaurant in its flagship Knightsbridge store and in September opened The Oxo Tower Restaurant on the south bank of the Thames.

The group spent 5.5 million stg in the first half on its Knightsbridge store and the development of the Oxo Tower. Morton said in the second half the group would make a nine million stg payment related to the new Leeds store opening, plus a further two million on a 4,000 extension of the menswear department at Knightsbridge.
Sales of "own bought" branded fashions increased by 14 percent in the half year and margins increased because the store sold more merchandise at full price and reduced markdowns.
The group reduced space devoted to "own bought" stock relative to concessions to 40 percent from 43 percent and the proportion of concession sales fell to 45 percent from 47 percent.
Morton said the group makes higher margins on own bought fashions than on the concessions and this helped improve margins on total fashion sales.

He said the group believed it had the balance between concessions and own bought about right for the Knightsbridge store. The Leeds store has about 30 percent concessions and 70 percent own bought merchandise, he said.
